hypotheses.text: GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder can be reliably discriminated from classical POLR3-related leukodystrophies (such as 4H leukodystrophy) by the absence of diffuse cerebral hypomyelination on T2-weighted MRI, presenting instead with focal midline structural defects (predominant cerebellar atrophy and corpus callosum dysgenesis) and preserved supratentorial myelin signal.
hypotheses.rationale: POLR3-related disorders typically present with hypomyelination, cerebellar atrophy, and hypodontia/hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. While GTF3C3 functions in the same transcriptional machinery (TFIIIC/RNA Pol III pathway), reported GTF3C3 cohorts show primary cerebellar atrophy, frontal hypoplasia, and callosal dysgenesis rather than classic diffuse white matter leukodystrophy signatures.

evidence.text: Brain imaging of four GTF3C3 patients revealed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, hypoplasia of frontal lobes, and simplified gyral pattern in one patient, without a primary presentation of diffuse hypomyelination.

source.title: White matter disorders at the intersection of transcription, RNA processing and translation
source.quote: Hereditary white matter disorders, encompassing leukodystrophies and genetically determined leukoencephalopathies, are a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by white matter signal abnormalities on neuroimaging.

hypotheses.text: The combination of progressive cerebellar atrophy with frontal lobe hypoplasia and corpus callosum dysgenesis constitutes a neuroimaging composite signature that discriminates GTF3C3 deficiency from other TFIIIC complex subunit disorders (such as GTF3C5), which exhibit prominent leukoencephalopathy rather than anterior forebrain structural hypoplasia.
hypotheses.rationale: Establishing whether distinct TFIIIC complex components generate distinct neuroarchitectural malformations is critical for clinical distinction prior to or following non-diagnostic exome sequencing.

evidence.text: A cohort of twelve individuals from 7 unrelated families demonstrated recurrent cerebellar and corpus callosum malformations associated with biallelic GTF3C3 missense variants.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: The cohort presented with intellectual disability, variable nonfamilial facial features, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations.

evidence.text: Structural brain imaging in GTF3C3 patients distinctly identified hypoplasia of frontal lobes alongside cerebellar atrophy.

hypotheses.text: Secondary cortical malformations, particularly simplified gyral pattern (HP:0009879), in GTF3C3-related disorder are specifically correlated with premature termination codons or compound heterozygous truncating/null alleles, whereas individuals with biallelic missense variants develop cerebellar and corpus callosum anomalies without cortical gyral simplification.
hypotheses.rationale: Simplified gyral pattern is reported only in a minority of patients (e.g., 1 of 4 in Abdel-Hamid et al., 2025 where a nonsense variant p.Arg717Ter was identified). Testing whether cortical migratory/organizational defects depend on severe loss of TFIIIC2 complex integrity will stratify phenotypic severity.

evidence.text: Out of 4 patients with biallelic variants including one nonsense allele (p.Arg717Ter), only one patient exhibited a moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern, while cerebellar involvement was observed across all imaged subjects.

new_directions.question_text: Does sequential longitudinal brain MRI in GTF3C3 patients show neurodegenerative progression of cerebellar atrophy, or is it a static congenital hypoplasia?
new_directions.rationale: Differentiating congenital cerebellar hypoplasia from progressive cerebellar atrophy is critical to distinguish GTF3C3 disorder from degenerative Pol III-related leukodystrophies and pontocerebellar hypoplasias.

new_directions.question_text: What is the incidence and radiological pattern of white matter involvement (hypomyelination vs. delayed myelination vs. normal myelination) across all published GTF3C3 cases?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether GTF3C3 should be classified as a primary leukoencephalopathy or purely a neuronal/structural malformation disorder will resolve ambiguities raised in recent reviews of transcription/translation-related white matter disorders.
